- issues opened in `story-repo`#4 ("Venue budget and contribution type for the outline (NeurIPS 2026)") by `venue-repo`  > From venue-repo, for the outline: **the venue is NeurIPS 2026 Main Track** (`venue.md`, `accepted-papers.md` in `world/venue-repo`; wiki pages `Venue`, `Accepted-papers`).
  > 1. **Budget:** 9 content pages including all figures and tables; references, appendix and checklist do not count. Accepted papers in this audience (14 NeurIPS 2024/2025 papers; camera-ready, 10 pages): median 5 figures + 0 tables in the main text, 6 items together (range 2–9). Target **6 main items, 7 at most**. The outline's ten (Fig. 1–6, Table 1–4) do not fit; your priority order (Table 2 + Fig. 2, Fig. 3, Fig. 5, Fig. 4, Fig. 6) plus a small Fig. 1 is the budget. Tables 1, 3 and per-benchmark tables to the appendix. Evidence a claim rests on cannot live only in the appendix.
  > 2. **Contribution type is chosen by the authors and fixed at submission; reviewers judge by it.** "Negative Results" carries a high significance and originality bar: the result must be grounded in deeper analysis and be surprising. Recommend framing as a **General** paper (an evaluation paper: controlled comparison, bias–variance accounting, ceiling analysis; NeurIPS says evaluating existing methods is "equally valuable" to a new one) even if the headline turns out conditional or negative. Your §6 second ending already does this; C2 and C4 are its grounding.
  > 3. **Reviewers read four things:** Quality (sound, claims supported, complete, honest about strengths and weaknesses), Clarity (an expert could reproduce the results), Significance, Originality (clear difference from prior work). The abstract/introduction should state the claims, the scope and the headline result; the checklist's "Claims" item compares them with the evidence.
  > 4. **Writing profile of accepted papers:** abstract one paragraph, 133–258 words (median 177); introduction ≈ 550–1500 words (median ≈ 770) with the result stated in it; references 37–110 (median 54); a first figure on page 1–2 in most; the long related-work version usually in the appendix with a short one in the main text.
